comment: The tests were quite manageable and the textbook he uses is really good as well. However, I wish he put more effort into explaining the concepts in his lectures. Linear algebra can be highly visual and applicable yet he mostly rushed through theorems from the textbook without any visualizations or further explanation.

Professor Nall does not cover the material well at all. I had to go through countless YouTube videos and rereading of the textbook to figure out what we were actually learning. However once you do figure out the topics, the tests are extremely easy. He gives you old tests and if you master those then you will be fine for every exam.

He does NOT teach you. You TEACH yourself math. The only plus side is he tells you what kind of questions will be on the Quiz and gives you past Hour exams that mirror what will be on the actual test. HOWEVER, don't go thinking he will tell you what will be on the Final.

You can clearly tell that Professor Nall knows math, and is very smart. However, he is really not good at teaching math, especially to students who just need the Gen Ed. His lectures are dense and hard to follow, and he will skip /leave out steps that he feels are "obvious". I learned everything from Webassign videos and my tutor.

This class is pretty much based off of exams and quizzes alone. I emailed him 16 times throughout the semester and never received a reply once. I asked for a homework extension so that I could work on it with my tutor and was denied. He is great if you are planning to major in math, but I would NEVER recommend taking him if you arent a math genius

Professor Van Nall's class was fine for me. Every class was either a lecture or a quiz/test I knew about beforehand. His lectures aren't the best, don't expect to learn much from them, but the HW will teach you most of everything on WebAssign. I never read the book, but the WebAssign instructional videos helped a lot.
Weekly quizzes. It's better to teach yourself if ur taking it with him .

He's really smart, but isn't good at explaining math. Reasonable amount of homework for the class, but I had to do a lot of reading the textbook to understand anything. You can skip most classes, except for the weekly quizzes.

This man is all over the place during lectures. Definitely loves math, but isn't so great at seeing things from students' perspectives. Moves through proofs very quickly and skips some steps that would help students follow his logic more easily.
He will tell you that he'll only put what he says he'll put on the test. That is a lie.

Dr. Nall is a pretty good professor at least for Abstract Math!! He gives daily hw that he never checks, but I suggest you do it, because it will help you for the exams. Also go to class, because sometimes he mistakenly gives solutions to projects. Lastly, he gives previous exams to review which are almost the same with the one he'll give you.

Dr. Nall really cares about math, but his lectures are not simple to understand. He will use technical terms and would give the feeling that its all so simple, instead of breaking it down and going to the depth. For math245, the textbook was good so it did the job. But do not expect to gain much from attending classes. An easy grader nonetheless.

Dr. Nall's lectures are incredibly difficult to keep up with. If you're looking to take Linear Algebra with him- take Multivariable Calc first. You will spend a lot of time figuring things out on your own with the textbook, but his quizzes and tests are very fair. He basically tells you what's on them, and does everything to boost your grade.

Dr. Nall is a brilliant professor who cares about his students. His lectures are really fast paced so get ready to read the textbook. He does not give clear explanations to complicated concepts though. However the best thing is his tests are super easy and he actually tells you what will be on the test. Take his course if you want an easy A.

Professor Nall is one of the smartest guys that I have ever met. He is extremely enthusiastic about math and inspired me to work hard. However, he moves very quickly, which often left me confused. If you ask questions you should be fine. In summary, you will have to work hard but you will learn a lot and be a better math student for it.

Don't take unless you like reading from the textbook. Van Nall's philosophy on teaching is to do examples without any explanation, like he expects you to already know the material. This class wouldn't be hard with a competent professor. He doesn't care if you understand the material. His lectures are cryptic, and boring. Avoid like the plague.
Gives you practice tests, not hard at all.

I took Multivariate Calculus, and it was my favorite class so far in college. It is not an easy subject, but if you try, Nall will give you the best grade possible for your work. A lot of the reviews are negative, but I feel that reflects more on the difficulty of the the course.   Nall is life.

Awesome guy, but he's the type to not understand why you couldn't possibly understand an abstract mathematical topic instantly.  Lectures were also very scattered and confusing, although interesting.  Basically taught myself out of the book the entire semester (which is an excellent one, by the way).

Dr. Nall is an extremely helpful and funny guy. And a great mathematician (he is an expert in topology). However, his lectures are hard to understand and he jumps here and there. But at least his tests are easy. It's easy to get a 100, but also easy to get an 80. Small mistakes on the test will lose you massive points. Extremely handsome guy though
Dr. Nall has a very loose, relaxed way of having class and discussion that end up making it like a Math seminar course - which is pretty dope.

I essentially taught myself the entire course. He was super helpful, but couldn't explain anything. I had already learned most of the material from taking physics courses, but he somehow managed to make me confused. His tests are very straightforward, no tricks at all, but know that you WILL have to read the book.

I taught myself the entire semester. His tests and weekly quizzes feel like they have nothing to do with what you're learning until the end of the year. You have to find someone to help you understand the concepts or you will fall behind.

Nall is not a very good professor.  He is a nice guy, but he speeds through lesson plans.  He explains the what of the course, but does not spend time on the why.  If you are good at calc already you will enjoy the class.  If you have not taken it you will probably struggle and I would look elsewhere.

He is a very nice person and willing to help, but the subject is challenging and he teaches fast. office hours are important. He is not a tough grader. do well on the weekly quizzes because they really help. Attendance is not mandatory but its necessary if you have never taken the course
easily best (and chillest) math prof ive had @ UR...material is tough but he presents it clearly

he is too busy playing with this tools in class and does not do a good job explaining the lesson! his notes are already pre-written in his computer that he just plays in class. this is not very helpful in teaching students who are learning calc3 for the first time.
This guy is great at explaining the lessons. You will learn it the first time if you pay attention.
goes over problems people had in the homework, if you understand all the homework and old tests and quizzes it is not too bad, although it is calculus

Van is a really nice guy but a little unclear though with his teachings and expectations.  He is very understanding with this though and will walk you through troublesome pts.  I would recommend him for Linear Algebra, i got an A.
he moves too quickly and mumbles when he explains problems

TERRIBLE at teaching- his examples were poor. tests were not too hard, but as someone who took calc in high school and did pretty good back then, i was disappointed with my semester grade. do your homework!

Dr. Nall posts old tests online so you know what to expect on tests, he wants everyone to get an A, and as long as you study you should be fine.  He is funny and will always help you outside of class- if you took calc in high school you'll get an A.

i'm in the middle of taking his class right now.  It started out shaky, but he's progressively doing better.  He is very helpul and his little quirks make class interesting.  Class goes by pretty fast.. the routine is always the same.  My only complaint is the lack of detail in which he goes through homework and lack of examples when teaching.

I've only had this man for 2 days, and I can already tell I'm in for a horrible grade because of him.  Nothing he teaches helps me on the homework and not even the book helps me with the homework.  He doesn't spend any time explaning anything and just keeps moving on, regardless of how lost everyone is.  I was good at calc before him...

unwilling to help, very unclear.  I think the problem is that he is so smart and he doesn't know how to transfer his knowledge to others.  Looks down upon his students and is very degrading if you don't understand.  His courses were difficult, but he didn't make them any easier because he was so hard to follow.  His tests came out of left field and most of class time was spent watching him try to do examples on the board.  He made what could have been interesting classes very boring and mundane.

Dr. Nall was a great prof for "Explloring Human Relations." Out of all my years at UR, I remember the most from this class with him. Even more than what I learned in my major field of Political Science.

Well, he's a cool guy, but he's kind of unclear about a lot of concepts and sometimes it's not even worth listening because he only contradicts himself.  Overall, he's a decent teacher and cares about his students for the most part.

Terrible teacher.  Lost half a semester's homework.  Didn't even write his own tests.  See previous comment about his "examples" that are incorrect homework problems and borrowed problem sets from other teachers.  Probably brilliant but shouldn't be in front of students.

He teaches by examples, but doesn't prepare any of these examples ahead of time.  Half of the class is often spent watching him try to figure out how to do his own problem that he just made up on the spot and then correcting a bunch of mistakes that he makes.  You have to teach yourself everything.
If you like hating math, or if you are a sadomasochist take him. Otherwise, choose another prof
He's basically a rocket scientist, really smart, kinda over your head sometimes.
nice man, terrible teacher. uniquely boring with little to no personality. take him if you do hw and like to teach yourself
No Comments
Really nice, and gives alot of points for going to office hours. However he is really unclear and hard to follow in class.
SO confusing, take him if you like teaching yourself
H.S. calc made no sense to me, but taking it with Nall was great. He is super nice and was very helpful outside of class. His final was also super-easy.

very dry, except on rare occassions when he has so much chalk all over his hands/shirt/pants that everyone starts laughing....the class is very difficult too...you have to take a lot of time out of class working on problems
